name: Hand-canvassed tailoring
summary: The tailor builds the chest of a coat from layers of hair canvas, shaped and stitched by hand, so that the coat holds its roll and fits the body.
how: Cut the canvas from horsehair and wool cloth, and shape it with the iron.
Pad-stitch the canvas to the cloth of the chest with small diagonal stitches, so that the lapel rolls.
Sew the shoulder, the collar and the lining by hand, and press the shape into the coat.

origin.note: London tailors of the Regency build the coat on canvas, so that the plain cloth shows a clean chest.

adoptions.via: The Savile Row houses make full-canvas coats to measure for the clubs and the court.
